# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names

# AI Teammate — GitHub-issues machine runner (TEMPLATE).
#
# Copy into the TARGET repository (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml) and
# adapt the RUNNER_* entries. This is the trimmed generic variant of the
# battle-tested machine-kit workflow (see epam/dmtools-dart
# .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml for the full reference with comments).
#
# Two entry paths, and BOTH must survive for the loop to be self-healing:
#   1. issues: [assigned, labeled] — the fast path (labels added with a
#      real PAT fire events; GITHUB_TOKEN-added labels do NOT — that is
#      exactly what the SM cron covers)
#   2. workflow_dispatch (issue / leg / reason) — the SM dispatch path:
#      the reconciler fires this directly, so mute labels cannot stall the
#      loop
#
# The guard derives the leg: dispatch input leg > label agent:rework >
# label agent:review > assignee/agent:dev (dev). Each leg runs the dmtools
# agent config named by RUNNER_*: dev (story/bug) develops from the issue
# body, review produces a machine PR review verdict, rework fixes the
# linked PR by the review threads.
name: 'AI Teammate'

# Run title carries the EFFECTIVE anchor (owner 2026-09-27, live: dmd run
# 36333172145): a PR-anchored SM dispatch (#544/#687 — inputs.pr set,
# inputs.issue empty) must title '▶ rework (SM) · pr-266', never the
# malformed '▶ rework (SM) · gh- · gh-: '. (inputs.pr || '') guards the
# label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
# render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (#544/#687) — the SM dispatches review/rework with pr instead of issue when the PR has no resolvable LOCAL issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: write

env:
  AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
  # ── adapt per target repo ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  RUNNER_STORY: dmtools-agents/story_development.json
  RUNNER_BUG: dmtools-agents/bug_development.json
  RUNNER_REVIEW: dmtools-agents/pr_review.json
  RUNNER_REWORK: dmtools-agents/pr_rework.json
  DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF: main
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: v0.1.5
  FA_VERSION: latest
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Secrets expected: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT), plus the AI provider key
  # referenced by the runner configs (e.g. ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY).

jobs:
  guard:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. Without this job-level gate the
    # guard allocated a runner on each lifecycle-label write only to decide
    # run=false (the self-retrigger no-op burn). `assigned` and the arming
    # `labeled` events (agent:*) still enter; lifecycle labels skip the job
    # entirely and never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned') ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
    steps:
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          INPUT_LEG: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
            LABELS="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')"
            ASSIGNEES="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"
          fi
          state="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state)"
          if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:skip"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          runner=""
          if [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "rework" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "review" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "dev" ]; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"
            fi
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:rework"; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:review"; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif echo "$ASSIGNEES" | grep -qw "$AGENT_HANDLE" || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:dev"; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"
            fi
          fi
          if [ -n "$runner" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "runner=$runner" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "kind=$(echo "$runner" | grep -q review && echo review || (echo "$runner" | grep -q rework && echo rework || echo dev))" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  teammate:
    needs: guard
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:

      # issue body to input/ticket.md, then:
      #   dmtools run "$RUNNER" '{"params":{"ticketKey":"gh-<n>"}}'

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1089
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1089
- **Title**: gh-1075 [GOAL] Fork PR dispatch: trigger on base ref + checkout refs/pull/N/head — cross-repo PRs are permanently undispatchable today (live: fa #1591 re-parked after rescue)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1075` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +619
- **Deletions**: -46
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T07:06:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T07:27:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1075
### What changed
Cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: a head-targeted dispatch for a fork PR reroutes onto the base repo's standard machine ref (`main`) with the PR number and a `refs/pull/<N>/head` checkout plan in the run inputs, instead of dispatching on the fork branch which 422s forever in the base repo (live fa pr-1591). The no-ref bookkeeping now keys fork heads to the `refs/pull/<N>/head` liveness probe instead of the branch name.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/forkDispatch.js`: `dispatchPlan` (fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PRs unchanged), `classifyForkNoRef`, `forkFullOf` (reuses the gh-1070 `validationLiveness.forkHeadFull` case-insensitive same-repo compare — no second resolver).
- `triggerWorkflow` applies the plan before dispatch and backfills `inputs.pr` only when the rule carried no `{prNumber}`; the gh-1028 branch-leg guard keeps its pre-gh-1075 semantics via a captured `headRefDispatch` flag.
- `recordDispatchFailure`: a no-ref failure on a fork PR runs an `ls-remote refs/pull/<N>/head` probe (fail-open to LIVE) — fetchable → never head-dead, no markers/park (AC2); unfetchable → parks through the existing gh-922 path keyed on the pull ref (AC3). Same-repo bookkeeping is byte-identical (REG-1); the gh-1028/715/1029 guards and the leg push-back (#1070 contract) are untouched.
- Leg checkout/push consumption of the `checkout_ref` input is deliberately out of scope (card non-goals; #1074 owns failure observability).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_forkDispatch.json   # UT-1/UT-2 pure contract (12 tests)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json        # IT-1/AC2/AC3/REG-1 tick suites (623 tests)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite — 4594 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Dispatch flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SM[SM tick: fork PR candidate] --> PLAN[forkDispatch.dispatchPlan]
  PLAN -->|same-repo| BR[ref: branch — unchanged]
  PLAN -->|cross-repo| MAIN[ref: main + inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/N/head]
  MAIN --> LEG[leg runs base workflow, checks out refs/pull/N/head]
  MAIN -. 422 no-ref .-> PROBE[ls-remote refs/pull/N/head]
  PROBE -->|fetchable| OK[not head-dead — no markers, no park]
  PROBE -->|unfetchable| PARK[gh-922 park keyed on the pull ref]
```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1089._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js` line 756

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-19):
# 🚨 BLOCKING: `checkout_ref` is not a declared input of the leg workflow — GitHub 422s the fork dispatch with "Unexpected inputs provided", so the fix cannot fire in production

The rerouted fork dispatch now sends `inputs.checkout_ref` (`js/smAgent.js:756`, and a backfilled `inputs.pr` at :757 when the rule carries no `{prNumber}`), but the workflow it targets declares no such input. The dispatch target is the **target repo's** `ai-teammate.yml` — every deployment of it is a copy of this repo's `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`, whose `workflow_dispatch` block declares exactly four inputs: `issue`, `leg`, `reason`, `pr` (`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template:45-67`). A repo-wide grep confirms `checkout_ref` exists nowhere in any workflow YAML — only in `smAgent.js` and the tests.

GitHub's dispatches REST endpoint validates the `inputs` object against the workflow file's declared inputs and rejects undeclared keys with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — documented live in [github/gh-aw#50027](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/50027) (`Failed to dispatch workflow "…": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]` on `POST …/dispatches` — 422, fixed by stripping undeclared keys before sending).

The consequence chain makes AC1 worse than unmet:

1. The dispatch no longer 422s with "No ref found" (the rerouted ref is `main`, which exists) — it 422s with "Unexpected inputs provided: ["checkout_ref"]" **on every tick**.
2. `triggerFailures.classifyTriggerError` (`js/common/triggerFailures.js:56`) only maps "no ref found"-shaped messages to `'no-ref'`; this message classifies as `'transient'`.
3. So `recordDispatchFailure` returns at the `failClass !== 'no-ref'` gate — **no probe, no markers, no park, only a console warning**. A fork PR is still permanently undispatchable, but now with zero observability — strictly worse than the gh-922 state this card fixes.

The PR description defers "leg checkout/push **consumption** of the `checkout_ref` input" as out of scope — but *declaring* the input is not consumption; without a declaration the dispatch is rejected before any leg code runs, so IT-1 ("dispatch fires once") can never hold against the real GitHub endpoint. The IT-1 test passes only because `onTrigger` is mocked and never sees GitHub's input validation.

**Fix**: declare `checkout_ref` (and document `pr`) in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`'s `workflow_dispatch` inputs (consumption can stay in the #1074 lane), and add a workflow-lint/unit assertion so a future undeclared dispatch input fails CI instead of silently 422ing. Until then, `recommendation` stays REQUEST_CHANGES.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js` line 678

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-19):
# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the gh-1028 single-writer leg guard is blind for rerouted fork dispatches — the run's `head_branch` is now `main`, not the fork branch

`headRefDispatch` preserves the guard's firing condition, but the guard's probe key — `it0.branch`, the fork branch name — no longer matches anything in the run list once the dispatch is rerouted. A `workflow_dispatch` run's `head_branch` is the dispatch ref (`main` after this PR), while `hasActiveLegRunOnBranch` still asks for runs whose `head_branch IS the dispatch branch` (`js/smAgent.js:678` → `:397` → `branchLegGuardModule.hasActiveLegRunOnBranch(runs, branch, …)`).

So for a fork PR the gh-1028 suppression can never see an in-flight leg: if both rework arms match the same fork PR (the issue-anchored rework-on-red-ci and the PR-anchored rework-on-label, exactly the gh-1028 live pathology on PR #1017), both dispatch, and two rework legs race the same fork head — with #1070 maintainer-edit pushes landing in the *fork*, the same double-push race gh-1028 was built to prevent. (Pre-gh-1075 this was latent because fork dispatches always 422'd; once the dispatch blocker is fixed this becomes live.)

Please key the probe on the pull ref (or `pr-<N>`) when `forkPlan.checkoutRef` is set — e.g. pass `forkPlan.checkoutRef || it0.branch` to `hasActiveLegRunOnBranch` — and add a regression test: fork PR + one in-flight leg run whose `head_branch` is `main` + a second dispatch arm → suppressed.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/smAgent.js` line 848

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-19):
# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the pull-ref liveness probe is unauthenticated — on private base repos it always fails closed to "live" and AC3 parking silently never fires

`forkPullRefLive` probes `git ls-remote https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git refs/pull/<N>/head` with no credentials (`js/smAgent.js:848`). For a private base repo (the common case for machine targets) this errors with "Repository not found" on every probe; the catch then returns `true` (fail-open, per the gh-922 blind-tick invariant) — so a genuinely dead fork head on a private repo is **never** classified 'dead', never accumulates markers, never parks. AC3 ("genuinely dead fork heads still park") is silently void exactly where most of the fleet runs.

The rest of this codebase probes the *runner's authenticated remote* instead of a hardcoded public URL: `js/prepareTestPRForReview.js:214` (`git ls-remote --heads origin …`), `js/prepareCliTestReworkSetup.js:106`, `js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js:81` — the SM runs in a checkout of the base repo where `origin` already carries the token (cf. the `GH_TOKEN` push-URL handling at `js/smAgent.js:2037`).

**Fix**: probe `origin` (or a token-bearing URL assembled from split literals the way the existing push URLs are, so the token never appears contiguously in source): `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/<N>/head`. Keep the fail-open catch as-is. A unit test with a private-repo-shaped probe error (auth failure) asserting "never parks but logs a distinct degraded warning" would pin the intent.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/smAgent.js` line 820

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-19):
# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the "fork deleted entirely" shape (`headRepo: null`) never reaches the pull-ref probe — the doc comment and the AC3 "keyed on the pull ref" claim don't hold for it

`forkDispatch.forkFullOf` fails closed to same-repo when `headRepo` is null, and the module comment (`js/common/forkDispatch.js:47-53`) names exactly that shape — "a deleted fork's REST payload carries head.repo:null" — as what "parks through the pull-ref probe". But with `headRepo` null the probe path here is **unreachable**:

1. `dispatchPlan` also sees `forkFullOf === null` → the plan is **not** rerouted → the dispatch still targets the fork branch → 422 "No ref found for: <fork-branch>".
2. Back in `recordDispatchFailure`, `forkFullOf(item, …)` is again null → the code drops to the same-repo branch (`js/smAgent.js:836`) → `expandedRef === item.branch` holds → `recordNoRefBookkeeping` keys the marker/park on the **branch name**, and no `ls-remote` probe ever runs.

So for the deleted-fork shape the AC3 outcome (a park) still happens — but through the pre-gh-1075 branch-keyed path, not "the existing no-ref path, keyed on the pull ref" as AC3 and the PR description state, and with no test coverage (every AC3 test keeps `headRepo: FORK_FULL` populated). Two consistency asks:

- Either route the null-`headRepo` + no-ref shape into the pull-ref probe (e.g. when `expandedRef === item.branch` and the branch is unfetchable on the base remote, treat as fork-suspect and probe `refs/pull/<N>/head`) — this also fixes a side effect: with the plan un-rerouted, a fork branch whose name collides with an existing base branch would dispatch on the *base* branch and validate the wrong code;
- or fix the comment/PR description/tests to state that the pull-ref-keyed park covers only the populated-`headRepo` case and the deleted-fork case parks branch-keyed via the legacy path.

Not blocking — parking still occurs — but the contract text and the tests currently describe a probe path the deleted-fork shape cannot reach.

---

# gh-1075: [GOAL] Fork PR dispatch: trigger on base ref + checkout refs/pull/N/head — cross-repo PRs are permanently undispatchable today (live: fa #1591 re-parked after rescue)

## Description

## Goal — cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: trigger on a base ref, check out refs/pull/N/head (v1)

One sentence: **a fork PR's legs run like any other PR's legs** — the SM dispatches the workflow on a base-repo ref with the PR number as input and the leg checks out `refs/pull/<N>/head` — instead of dispatching with `ref: <fork-branch>` which 422s forever.

Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — after the dead-head park fix (#1057, merged) and the fork-aware silent-update (#1070, merged), the THIRD fork-blind lane surfaced: the dispatch itself. Tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z: `pr-1591 dispatch dead-head (5/3 no-ref failures on fix/android-dap-home-sandbox) — validation_failed park`. The branch lives in the fork; `workflow_dispatch` with `ref: fix/android-dap-home-sandbox` in the base repo can never resolve → 422 "No ref found" → the gh-922 no-ref bookkeeping parks the PR — and because the park post-dates the last human push, the head-change reset never clears it. A fork PR is permanently undispatchable; every guest contribution dead-ends here.

## Root cause

`recordDispatchFailure` (js/smAgent.js:755+) treats a 422 on `ref: <branch>` as head-dead evidence — correct for same-repo PRs, structurally wrong for cross-repo PRs where the branch NEVER exists in the base repo. The dispatch contract itself (`ref: <head branch>`) assumes the branch is base-local.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Dispatch for a cross-repo PR triggers the workflow on the base default branch (or the repo's standard machine ref) with the PR number carried in inputs; the leg's checkout step resolves `refs/pull/<N>/head` (always fetchable, even when the fork branch is deleted). Same-repo PRs keep today's `ref: <branch>` dispatch (regression guard).
- **AC2** — A 422 no-ref failure on a cross-repo PR is never classified as head-dead (the head's liveness oracle for forks is `refs/pull/<N>/head`, per #1057) — no trigger-failure markers, no park accumulation.
- **AC3** — Genuinely dead fork heads (PR head ref unfetchable — fork deleted entirely) still park via the existing no-ref path, keyed to the pull-ref probe instead of the branch name.
- **AC4** — The leg's push-back path for fork PRs follows #1070's maintainer-edit contract (probe → push to fork / guest-park fallback) — no new push logic invented here.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — dispatch ref selection: fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PR → head branch (pure function, stubbed PR payloads).
- `UT-2` — no-ref classification: 422 on a fork branch name → NOT head-dead; unfetchable pull ref → head-dead (AC2/AC3).
- `IT-1` — simulated tick with a fork PR candidate: dispatch fires once, no park labels, checkout plan in the run inputs (AC1).
- `REG-1` — gh-922 bookkeeping tests (same-repo no-ref park after cap) stay green unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Running legs FROM the fork's workflow copy (untrusted code path — legs always run the base repo's workflow, checking out only the PR's data).
- Auto-merging fork PRs with failing validation (validation still required; this card only makes the legs runnable).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z ("dispatch dead-head 5/3 no-ref")
- js/smAgent.js recordDispatchFailure (:755+), js/sm/sources/githubSource.js no-ref classification (:141, :1136)
- Sibling fork-blindness cards: #1057 (park oracle — merged), #1070 (silent-update — merged), #1074 (failure observability)

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

# AI Teammate — GitHub-issues machine runner (TEMPLATE).
#
# Copy into the TARGET repository (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml) and
# adapt the RUNNER_* entries. This is the trimmed generic variant of the
# battle-tested machine-kit workflow (see epam/dmtools-dart
# .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml for the full reference with comments).
#
# Two entry paths, and BOTH must survive for the loop to be self-healing:
#   1. issues: [assigned, labeled] — the fast path (labels added with a
#      real PAT fire events; GITHUB_TOKEN-added labels do NOT — that is
#      exactly what the SM cron covers)
#   2. workflow_dispatch (issue / leg / reason) — the SM dispatch path:
#      the reconciler fires this directly, so mute labels cannot stall the
#      loop
#
# The guard derives the leg: dispatch input leg > label agent:rework >
# label agent:review > assignee/agent:dev (dev). Each leg runs the dmtools
# agent config named by RUNNER_*: dev (story/bug) develops from the issue
# body, review produces a machine PR review verdict, rework fixes the
# linked PR by the review threads.
name: 'AI Teammate'

# Run title carries the EFFECTIVE anchor (owner 2026-09-27, live: dmd run
# 36333172145): a PR-anchored SM dispatch (#544/#687 — inputs.pr set,
# inputs.issue empty) must title '▶ rework (SM) · pr-266', never the
# malformed '▶ rework (SM) · gh- · gh-: '. (inputs.pr || '') guards the
# label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
# render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (#544/#687) — the SM dispatches review/rework with pr instead of issue when the PR has no resolvable LOCAL issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: write

env:
  AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
  # ── adapt per target repo ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  RUNNER_STORY: dmtools-agents/story_development.json
  RUNNER_BUG: dmtools-agents/bug_development.json
  RUNNER_REVIEW: dmtools-agents/pr_review.json
  RUNNER_REWORK: dmtools-agents/pr_rework.json
  DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF: main
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: v0.1.5
  FA_VERSION: latest
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Secrets expected: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT), plus the AI provider key
  # referenced by the runner configs (e.g. ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY).

jobs:
  guard:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. Without this job-level gate the
    # guard allocated a runner on each lifecycle-label write only to decide
    # run=false (the self-retrigger no-op burn). `assigned` and the arming
    # `labeled` events (agent:*) still enter; lifecycle labels skip the job
    # entirely and never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned') ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
    steps:
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          INPUT_LEG: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
            LABELS="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')"
            ASSIGNEES="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"
          fi
          state="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state)"
          if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:skip"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          runner=""
          if [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "rework" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "review" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "dev" ]; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"
            fi
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:rework"; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:review"; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif echo "$ASSIGNEES" | grep -qw "$AGENT_HANDLE" || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:dev"; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"
            fi
          fi
          if [ -n "$runner" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "runner=$runner" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "kind=$(echo "$runner" | grep -q review && echo review || (echo "$runner" | grep -q rework && echo rework || echo dev))" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  teammate:
    needs: guard
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      # Adapt the runner steps from the machine-kit reference workflow:
      # checkout (target + dmtools-agents), install dmtools + fa, write the
      # issue body to input/ticket.md, then:
      #   dmtools run "$RUNNER" '{"params":{"ticketKey":"gh-<n>"}}'
      # Fu…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1089
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1089
- **Title**: gh-1075 [GOAL] Fork PR dispatch: trigger on base ref + checkout refs/pull/N/head — cross-repo PRs are permanently undispatchable today (live: fa #1591 re-parked after rescue)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1075` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +619
- **Deletions**: -46
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T07:06:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T07:27:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1075
### What changed
Cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: a head-targeted dispatch for a fork PR reroutes onto the base repo's standard machine ref (`main`) with the PR number and a `refs/pull/<N>/head` checkout plan in the run inputs, instead of dispatching on the fork branch which 422s forever in the base repo (live fa pr-1591). The no-ref bookkeeping now keys fork heads to the `refs/pull/<N>/head` liveness probe instead of the branch name.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/forkDispatch.js`: `dispatchPlan` (fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PRs unchanged), `classifyForkNoRef`, `forkFullOf` (reuses the gh-1070 `validationLiveness.forkHeadFull` case-insensitive same-repo compare — no second resolver).
- `triggerWorkflow` applies the plan before dispatch and backfills `inputs.pr` only when the rule carried no `{prNumber}`; the gh-1028 branch-leg guard keeps its pre-gh-1075 semantics via a captured `headRefDispatch` flag.
- `recordDispatchFailure`: a no-ref failure on a fork PR runs an `ls-remote refs/pull/<N>/head` probe (fail-open to LIVE) — fetchable → never head-dead, no markers/park (AC2); unfetchable → parks through the existing gh-922 path keyed on the pull ref (AC3). Same-repo bookkeeping is byte-identical (REG-1); the gh-1028/715/1029 guards and the leg push-back (#1070 contract) are untouched.
- Leg checkout/push consumption of the `checkout_ref` input is deliberately out of scope (card non-goals; #1074 owns failure observability).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_forkDispatch.json   # UT-1/UT-2 pure contract (12 tests)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json        # IT-1/AC2/AC3/REG-1 tick suites (623 tests)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite — 4594 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Dispatch flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SM[SM tick: fork PR candidate] --> PLAN[forkDispatch.dispatchPlan]
  PLAN -->|same-repo| BR[ref: branch — unchanged]
  PLAN -->|cross-repo| MAIN[ref: main + inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/N/head]
  MAIN --> LEG[leg runs base workflow, checks out refs/pull/N/head]
  MAIN -. 422 no-ref .-> PROBE[ls-remote refs/pull/N/head]
  PROBE -->|fetchable| OK[not head-dead — no markers, no park]
  PROBE -->|unfetchable| PARK[gh-922 park keyed on the pull ref]
```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1089._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js` line 756

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-19):
# 🚨 BLOCKING: `checkout_ref` is not a declared input of the leg workflow — GitHub 422s the fork dispatch with "Unexpected inputs provided", so the fix cannot fire in production

The rerouted fork dispatch now sends `inputs.checkout_ref` (`js/smAgent.js:756`, and a backfilled `inputs.pr` at :757 when the rule carries no `{prNumber}`), but the workflow it targets declares no such input. The dispatch target is the **target repo's** `ai-teammate.yml` — every deployment of it is a copy of this repo's `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`, whose `workflow_dispatch` block declares exactly four inputs: `issue`, `leg`, `reason`, `pr` (`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template:45-67`). A repo-wide grep confirms `checkout_ref` exists nowhere in any workflow YAML — only in `smAgent.js` and the tests.

GitHub's dispatches REST endpoint validates the `inputs` object against the workflow file's declared inputs and rejects undeclared keys with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — documented live in [github/gh-aw#50027](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/50027) (`Failed to dispatch workflow "…": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]` on `POST …/dispatches` — 422, fixed by stripping undeclared keys before sending).

The consequence chain makes AC1 worse than unmet:

1. The dispatch no longer 422s with "No ref found" (the rerouted ref is `main`, which exists) — it 422s with "Unexpected inputs provided: ["checkout_ref"]" **on every tick**.
2. `triggerFailures.classifyTriggerError` (`js/common/triggerFailures.js:56`) only maps "no ref found"-shaped messages to `'no-ref'`; this message classifies as `'transient'`.
3. So `recordDispatchFailure` returns at the `failClass !== 'no-ref'` gate — **no probe, no markers, no park, only a console warning**. A fork PR is still permanently undispatchable, but now with zero observability — strictly worse than the gh-922 state this card fixes.

The PR description defers "leg checkout/push **consumption** of the `checkout_ref` input" as out of scope — but *declaring* the input is not consumption; without a declaration the dispatch is rejected before any leg code runs, so IT-1 ("dispatch fires once") can never hold against the real GitHub endpoint. The IT-1 test passes only because `onTrigger` is mocked and never sees GitHub's input validation.

**Fix**: declare `checkout_ref` (and document `pr`) in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`'s `workflow_dispatch` inputs (consumption can stay in the #1074 lane), and add a workflow-lint/unit assertion so a future undeclared dispatch input fails CI instead of silently 422ing. Until then, `recommendation` stays REQUEST_CHANGES.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js` line 678

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-19):
# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the gh-1028 single-writer leg guard is blind for rerouted fork dispatches — the run's `head_branch` is now `main`, not the fork branch

`headRefDispatch` preserves the guard's firing condition, but the guard's probe key — `it0.branch`, the fork branch name — no longer matches anything in the run list once the dispatch is rerouted. A `workflow_dispatch` run's `head_branch` is the dispatch ref (`main` after this PR), while `hasActiveLegRunOnBranch` still asks for runs whose `head_branch IS the dispatch branch` (`js/smAgent.js:678` → `:397` → `branchLegGuardModule.hasActiveLegRunOnBranch(runs, branch, …)`).

So for a fork PR the gh-1028 suppression can never see an in-flight leg: if both rework arms match the same fork PR (the issue-anchored rework-on-red-ci and the PR-anchored rework-on-label, exactly the gh-1028 live pathology on PR #1017), both dispatch, and two rework legs race the same fork head — with #1070 maintainer-edit pushes landing in the *fork*, the same double-push race gh-1028 was built to prevent. (Pre-gh-1075 this was latent because fork dispatches always 422'd; once the dispatch blocker is fixed this becomes live.)

Please key the probe on the pull ref (or `pr-<N>`) when `forkPlan.checkoutRef` is set — e.g. pass `forkPlan.checkoutRef || it0.branch` to `hasActiveLegRunOnBranch` — and add a regression test: fork PR + one in-flight leg run whose `head_branch` is `main` + a second dispatch arm → suppressed.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/smAgent.js` line 848

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-19):
# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the pull-ref liveness probe is unauthenticated — on private base repos it always fails closed to "live" and AC3 parking silently never fires

`forkPullRefLive` probes `git ls-remote https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git refs/pull/<N>/head` with no credentials (`js/smAgent.js:848`). For a private base repo (the common case for machine targets) this errors with "Repository not found" on every probe; the catch then returns `true` (fail-open, per the gh-922 blind-tick invariant) — so a genuinely dead fork head on a private repo is **never** classified 'dead', never accumulates markers, never parks. AC3 ("genuinely dead fork heads still park") is silently void exactly where most of the fleet runs.

The rest of this codebase probes the *runner's authenticated remote* instead of a hardcoded public URL: `js/prepareTestPRForReview.js:214` (`git ls-remote --heads origin …`), `js/prepareCliTestReworkSetup.js:106`, `js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js:81` — the SM runs in a checkout of the base repo where `origin` already carries the token (cf. the `GH_TOKEN` push-URL handling at `js/smAgent.js:2037`).

**Fix**: probe `origin` (or a token-bearing URL assembled from split literals the way the existing push URLs are, so the token never appears contiguously in source): `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/<N>/head`. Keep the fail-open catch as-is. A unit test with a private-repo-shaped probe error (auth failure) asserting "never parks but logs a distinct degraded warning" would pin the intent.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/smAgent.js` line 820

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-19):
# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the "fork deleted entirely" shape (`headRepo: null`) never reaches the pull-ref probe — the doc comment and the AC3 "keyed on the pull ref" claim don't hold for it

`forkDispatch.forkFullOf` fails closed to same-repo when `headRepo` is null, and the module comment (`js/common/forkDispatch.js:47-53`) names exactly that shape — "a deleted fork's REST payload carries head.repo:null" — as what "parks through the pull-ref probe". But with `headRepo` null the probe path here is **unreachable**:

1. `dispatchPlan` also sees `forkFullOf === null` → the plan is **not** rerouted → the dispatch still targets the fork branch → 422 "No ref found for: <fork-branch>".
2. Back in `recordDispatchFailure`, `forkFullOf(item, …)` is again null → the code drops to the same-repo branch (`js/smAgent.js:836`) → `expandedRef === item.branch` holds → `recordNoRefBookkeeping` keys the marker/park on the **branch name**, and no `ls-remote` probe ever runs.

So for the deleted-fork shape the AC3 outcome (a park) still happens — but through the pre-gh-1075 branch-keyed path, not "the existing no-ref path, keyed on the pull ref" as AC3 and the PR description state, and with no test coverage (every AC3 test keeps `headRepo: FORK_FULL` populated). Two consistency asks:

- Either route the null-`headRepo` + no-ref shape into the pull-ref probe (e.g. when `expandedRef === item.branch` and the branch is unfetchable on the base remote, treat as fork-suspect and probe `refs/pull/<N>/head`) — this also fixes a side effect: with the plan un-rerouted, a fork branch whose name collides with an existing base branch would dispatch on the *base* branch and validate the wrong code;
- or fix the comment/PR description/tests to state that the pull-ref-keyed park covers only the populated-`headRepo` case and the deleted-fork case parks branch-keyed via the legacy path.

Not blocking — parking still occurs — but the contract text and the tests currently describe a probe path the deleted-fork shape cannot reach.

---

# gh-1075: [GOAL] Fork PR dispatch: trigger on base ref + checkout refs/pull/N/head — cross-repo PRs are permanently undispatchable today (live: fa #1591 re-parked after rescue)

## Description

## Goal — cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: trigger on a base ref, check out refs/pull/N/head (v1)

One sentence: **a fork PR's legs run like any other PR's legs** — the SM dispatches the workflow on a base-repo ref with the PR number as input and the leg checks out `refs/pull/<N>/head` — instead of dispatching with `ref: <fork-branch>` which 422s forever.

Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — after the dead-head park fix (#1057, merged) and the fork-aware silent-update (#1070, merged), the THIRD fork-blind lane surfaced: the dispatch itself. Tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z: `pr-1591 dispatch dead-head (5/3 no-ref failures on fix/android-dap-home-sandbox) — validation_failed park`. The branch lives in the fork; `workflow_dispatch` with `ref: fix/android-dap-home-sandbox` in the base repo can never resolve → 422 "No ref found" → the gh-922 no-ref bookkeeping parks the PR — and because the park post-dates the last human push, the head-change reset never clears it. A fork PR is permanently undispatchable; every guest contribution dead-ends here.

## Root cause

`recordDispatchFailure` (js/smAgent.js:755+) treats a 422 on `ref: <branch>` as head-dead evidence — correct for same-repo PRs, structurally wrong for cross-repo PRs where the branch NEVER exists in the base repo. The dispatch contract itself (`ref: <head branch>`) assumes the branch is base-local.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Dispatch for a cross-repo PR triggers the workflow on the base default branch (or the repo's standard machine ref) with the PR number carried in inputs; the leg's checkout step resolves `refs/pull/<N>/head` (always fetchable, even when the fork branch is deleted). Same-repo PRs keep today's `ref: <branch>` dispatch (regression guard).
- **AC2** — A 422 no-ref failure on a cross-repo PR is never classified as head-dead (the head's liveness oracle for forks is `refs/pull/<N>/head`, per #1057) — no trigger-failure markers, no park accumulation.
- **AC3** — Genuinely dead fork heads (PR head ref unfetchable — fork deleted entirely) still park via the existing no-ref path, keyed to the pull-ref probe instead of the branch name.
- **AC4** — The leg's push-back path for fork PRs follows #1070's maintainer-edit contract (probe → push to fork / guest-park fallback) — no new push logic invented here.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — dispatch ref selection: fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PR → head branch (pure function, stubbed PR payloads).
- `UT-2` — no-ref classification: 422 on a fork branch name → NOT head-dead; unfetchable pull ref → head-dead (AC2/AC3).
- `IT-1` — simulated tick with a fork PR candidate: dispatch fires once, no park labels, checkout plan in the run inputs (AC1).
- `REG-1` — gh-922 bookkeeping tests (same-repo no-ref park after cap) stay green unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Running legs FROM the fork's workflow copy (untrusted code path — legs always run the base repo's workflow, checking out only the PR's data).
- Auto-merging fork PRs with failing validation (validation still required; this card only makes the legs runnable).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z ("dispatch dead-head 5/3 no-ref")
- js/smAgent.js recordDispatchFailure (:755+), js/sm/sources/githubSource.js no-ref classification (:141, :1136)
- Sibling fork-blindness cards: #1057 (park oracle — merged), #1070 (silent-update — merged), #1074 (failure observability)

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

# malformed '▶ rework (SM) · gh- · gh-: '. (inputs.pr || '') guards the
# label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
# render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (#544/#687) — the SM dispatches review/rework with pr instead of issue when the PR has no resolvable LOCAL issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: write

env:

  # Secrets expected: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT), plus the AI provider key

jobs:

    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. Without this job-level gate the
    # guard allocated a runner on each lifecycle-label write only to decide
    # run=false (the self-retrigger no-op burn). `assigned` and the arming
    # `labeled` events (agent:*) still enter; lifecycle labels skip the job
    # entirely and never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned') ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:

      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}

    steps:

        id: check
        env:

          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          INPUT_LEG: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
            LABELS="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')"
            ASSIGNEES="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"
          fi

          if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi

            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi

          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "dev" ]; then

            fi

          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:review"; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif echo "$ASSIGNEES" | grep -qw "$AGENT_HANDLE" || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:dev"; then

            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"
            fi
          fi
          if [ -n "$runner" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "runner=$runner" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "kind=$(echo "$runner" | grep -q review && echo review || (echo "$runner" | grep -q rework && echo rework || echo dev))" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

# gh-1075: [GOAL] Fork PR dispatch: trigger on base ref + checkout refs/pull/N/head — cross-repo PRs are permanently undispatchable today (live: fa #1591 re-parked after rescue)

## Description

## Goal — cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: trigger on a base ref, check out refs/pull/N/head (v1)

One sentence: **a fork PR's legs run like any other PR's legs** — the SM dispatches the workflow on a base-repo ref with the PR number as input and the leg checks out `refs/pull/<N>/head` — instead of dispatching with `ref: <fork-branch>` which 422s forever.

Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — after the dead-head park fix (#1057, merged) and the fork-aware silent-update (#1070, merged), the THIRD fork-blind lane surfaced: the dispatch itself. Tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z: `pr-1591 dispatch dead-head (5/3 no-ref failures on fix/android-dap-home-sandbox) — validation_failed park`. The branch lives in the fork; `workflow_dispatch` with `ref: fix/android-dap-home-sandbox` in the base repo can never resolve → 422 "No ref found" → the gh-922 no-ref bookkeeping parks the PR — and because the park post-dates the last human push, the head-change reset never clears it. A fork PR is permanently undispatchable; every guest contribution dead-ends here.

## Root cause

`recordDispatchFailure` (js/smAgent.js:755+) treats a 422 on `ref: <branch>` as head-dead evidence — correct for same-repo PRs, structurally wrong for cross-repo PRs where the branch NEVER exists in the base repo. The dispatch contract itself (`ref: <head branch>`) assumes the branch is base-local.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Dispatch for a cross-repo PR triggers the workflow on the base default branch (or the repo's standard machine ref) with the PR number carried in inputs; the leg's checkout step resolves `refs/pull/<N>/head` (always fetchable, even when the fork branch is deleted). Same-repo PRs keep today's `ref: <branch>` dispatch (regression guard).
- **AC2** — A 422 no-ref failure on a cross-repo PR is never classified as head-dead (the head's liveness oracle for forks is `refs/pull/<N>/head`, per #1057) — no trigger-failure markers, no park accumulation.
- **AC3** — Genuinely dead fork heads (PR head ref unfetchable — fork deleted entirely) still park via the existing no-ref path, keyed to the pull-ref probe instead of the branch name.
- **AC4** — The leg's push-back path for fork PRs follows #1070's maintainer-edit contract (probe → push to fork / guest-park fallback) — no new push logic invented here.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — dispatch ref selection: fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PR → head branch (pure function, stubbed PR payloads).
- `UT-2` — no-ref classification: 422 on a fork branch name → NOT head-dead; unfetchable pull ref → head-dead (AC2/AC3).
- `IT-1` — simulated tick with a fork PR candidate: dispatch fires once, no park labels, checkout plan in the run inputs (AC1).
- `REG-1` — gh-922 bookkeeping tests (same-repo no-ref park after cap) stay green unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Running legs FROM the fork's workflow copy (untrusted code path — legs always run the base repo's workflow, checking out only the PR's data).
- Auto-merging fork PRs with failing validation (validation still required; this card only makes the legs runnable).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z ("dispatch dead-head 5/3 no-ref")
- js/smAgent.js recordDispatchFailure (:755+), js/sm/sources/githubSource.js no-ref classification (:141, :1136)
- Sibling fork-blindness cards: #1057 (park oracle — merged), #1070 (silent-update — merged), #1074 (failure observability)

- [x] ▶ review (fa-review) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39213897805) · started 07:07 · done 07:23 ✅

+/**
+ * Fork-PR dispatch contract (gh-1075) — the pure half of the SM's
+ * cross-repo dispatch lane.
+ *
+ * Live fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) 2026-10-19T06:16Z: `pr-1591 dispatch
+ * dead-head (5/3 no-ref failures on fix/android-dap-home-sandbox) —
+ * validation_failed park`. The fork branch NEVER exists in the base repo,
+ * so a `workflow_dispatch` with `ref: <fork-branch>` answers 422 "No ref
